main_text.p: Sol: aurum. Dies fecundus ; cujus fignum סרטן Canter, Angelus Gabriel, minister לבנה Luna: argentum. Dies tertius; cujus fignum ועקרב טלה Aries & Scorpius, Angelus Samael, minister מאדים Mars. Dies quartus ; cujus fignum תאומים ובתולה Gemini & Virgo, Angelus Micael, minister כוכב Mercurius. Dies quintus ; cujus fignum קשת ורגים [?] Arcu-arius & Pifces, Angelus Tzadkiel, minister צדק Jupiter. Dies fextus ; cujus fignum שור ומאזנים Taurus & Libra, Angelus Anael, minister נוגה Venus : æs. Dies Sabbathi, cujus fignum גדי ודלי Capricornus & Aquarius, Angelus Kaphriel, minister שבתאי Saturnus. Nomina quorundam metallorum adjiciuntur, ex figmentis Alcumiftarum, qui ista planetarum nomina iis indidere. Hæc sunt inter גלולים ftercora domûs Ifraelis, tempore commiserationis abjicienda. Nec omni prorsus superstitione caret, quòd Schillerus in Cœlo ftellato Christiano, abolitâ istâ Gentili dierum nomenclaturâ, quam & nos etiamnum ore ferimus, primô die, ut rectè, Dominicô appellatô, pro die Lunæ, Spiritûs S. pro die Martis, Beatorum omnium; pro die Mercurij, Ecclesiæ Catholicæ; pro die Jovis, Cœnæ & Corporis Domini; pro die Veneris, Crucis ac Passionis Christi; pro die Saturni, Virginis Mariæ, audiri vellet.

§. 14. Israelitis olim singuli Hebdomadæ dies àSabbatho denominabantur: Ιt μία σαββάτων, prima Sabbathorum, Matth.28.1. Luc.24.1. Joh.20.1. Et Pharisæus ille, jejuno, inquit, δἰς τῷ σαββάτῳ bis per septimanam, Luc.18.12. Sic in Bab. Maccoth cap.1. fol.5.1. Dixit Rabba, venerunt duo, testes, dicentes; Sora, tempore matutino בחד בשבא primô Sabbathi פלוני N N. homicidium commisit. Venerunt duo, dicentes; בחד בשבא בפניא vesperi primô Sabbathi nobiscum fuistis Nahardea &c. Ita deinceps אלא בתרי בשבא sed

page.notes: Hebrew and Greek in the scan are small and partly hard to read; the Hebrew words in the planetary lines and the final lines are copied as best read. The "קשת ורגים" word and the Greek "δἰς τῷ σαββάτῳ" are doubtful. The text is cut off at the foot of the page, ending with the catchword-like "sed" set below the last Hebrew line, which is treated as running text.
